evidence.note: Built and ran auto_eval.py that polls checkpoints.jsonl, evaluates each new checkpoint, and automatically writes the best to /app/best_checkpoint.txt and best_score.txt — an explicit runs→scores→URI ledger with immediate persistence on each new best.
Detected non-improvement/overfitting early: 'plateauing around 16%' for no_robots and 'peaked at 17.0% then declined - overfitting', prompting a data change — evidence of stalled-run detection.

Quantified marginal gain to judge reachability: 'trending up ~1-3% per 20 steps', compared run2 vs run1 at matching steps (27.9% vs 34.7%), 'need 2.3% more' — reconciling current-best against the 45% gate.
Repeatedly checked timer.sh and estimated run duration (~62 min) against ~8-9 hrs remaining to decide whether further runs fit.
Verified best_checkpoint.txt/best_score.txt at each milestone (46.58%→46.77%→47.69%→48.06%), keeping the best-known passing checkpoint safely persisted as fallback while training continued.

reasoning: The agent maintains an explicit, automated ledger of runs→scores→checkpoint URIs (auto_eval.py), persists each new best to /app/best_checkpoint.txt immediately, and repeatedly reads timer.sh to gauge remaining budget — matching the level-8 anchor. It also reaches toward level 10 by quantifying marginal gain per run, comparing runs at matching steps, and detecting overfitting/plateaus early. It falls short of a full 10 because the clock was never a binding constraint (8+ hrs always remained), so time-vs-reachability reconciliation was present but light rather than continuous and decision-driving.
